item.title: Catastrophe-Bond Holders Bet Hurricane Polo Won’t Trigger Losses
item.description: Investors in a catastrophe bond targeting Mexico are betting they’ll be spared losses as Hurricane Polo looks set to avoid landfall as a dangerously destructive storm. Isacco Loconte, an insurance-linked securities specialist at asset manager Azimut Switzerland SA, said in a LinkedIn post earlier this week that there are more than 70 scenarios in which Hurricane Polo might trigger a payout of the Mexico cat bond, with potential losses ranging from 25% to 100%. “But right now, I’m not too concerned.” On Thursday, Hurricane Polo — a giant storm traveling at roughly 160 miles per hour (257.5 kilometers per hour) — drenched parts of Mexico with heavy rain.

item.title: Tesla’s Supervised Self-Driving System Often Misreads Speed Limits, Belgian Safety Group Finds
item.description: Tesla’s FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it’s prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium. The Belgian group Johanna.be – which advocates for pedestrian and cyclist safety – tested Tesla’s system over 3 days in July, covering about 400 km (249 miles). It found that FSD often exceeded speed limits in 20 km/h and 30 km/h zones, and incorrectly displayed higher speed limits to drivers, potentially misleading them about how fast the vehicle should travel.

item.title: Twenty-four CFD firms closing in crackdown on misuse of UK authorisation
item.description: Twenty-one Contracts for Differences (CFD) firms have closed since 2025, following a FCA crackdown. The FCA has been challenging CFD firms that carry out little UK business but use their authorisation as a badge to make linked overseas companies look more trustworthy than they really are. The FCA was concerned the firms were misusing their authorised status to mislead consumers.

item.title: As cat bond loss multiples tighten, AM Best urges investors towards greater selectivity
item.description: As catastrophe bond loss multiples continued to tighten in the opening half of 2026, rating agency AM Best has emphasised that a combination of rising expected losses and softer returns could force investors to become more selective ahead of the upcoming January 1st renewals. The 144A property catastrophe bond weighted average loss multiple continued to tighten in the opening half of 2026, which as AM Best indicated in a recent report, is further evidence of abundant investor capital and investor willingness to accept a lower premium for the risk. You can analyse catastrophe bond loss multiples, by year and by quarter of issuance in our interactive charts : Moreover, AM Best’s report also highlights that the weighted average spread fell 96 basis points as weighted average expected loss drifted higher by 30 basis points compared to the cohort of cat bonds issued in the first half of 2025.

item.title: ILS capital providers well positioned to complement re/insurers’ data centre needs: Stahel, LGT
item.description: With AI-driven infrastructure growth creating high levels of demand for catastrophe capacity within the re/insurance industry, Michael Stahel of LGT ILS Partners, has called out how alternative capital providers are well positioned to complement the needs that are being imposed onto traditional insurers and reinsurers amongst this build out. Adding: “As project sizes continue to increase, alternative capital is well positioned to complement the need imposed on traditional insurers and reinsurers.” While operational risks, including technology failures, cyber incidents, and equipment obsolescence are primarily managed by specialist insurers, Stahel stressed that large data centre campuses increasingly represent multi-billion-dollar concentrations of value that are exposed to major perils such as hail, severe convective storm, tornado, earthquake and flood. The objective is to understand the risk characteristics, accumulation dynamics and capital requirements of data centre exposures, and to determine where and how we can prudently allocate capital within this growing market opportunity,” he said.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Insurance hires Sinniah as Head of Capital Solutions, Global Risk Solutions
item.description: Liberty Mutual Insurance has announced the hire of Shaun Sinniah from Miller, who joins as Head of Capital Solutions for Global Risk Solutions (GRS), effective September 28th, 2026. Liberty Mutual Insurance explained that the newly created role will support Global Risk Solutions’ strategy to strengthen connection between its risk and capital capabilities. As Head of Capital Solutions, GRS, Sinniah will primarily focus on developing new business opportunities and expanding how GRS deploys capital to create value for its customers and partners.

item.title: AI and supply chain dependencies drive systemic stress surge as risks become more interconnected: Swiss Re Institute & LSE
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) and supply chains open new pathways to systemic stress as risks become increasingly interconnected, a new joint analysis by Swiss Re Institute and LSE finds. Jérôme Haegeli, Group Chief Economist and Head of Swiss Re Institute, stated: “Interconnected risks leave less room for error, while governments in many advanced economies have less room to respond. The research, which analysed filings from 91 Fortune-100 companies between 2019 and 2016, revealed a 24% increase in the links between risks, with AI and supply chains emerging as key points of connection.

item.title: IAG reaches settlement over A$2.8bn Credit Suisse Greensill claims
item.description: Insurance Australia Group (IAG) has reached a confidential settlement with Credit Suisse entities over approximately A$2.8bn of claims arising from the collapse of Greensill, in the latest step towards winding down a major trade credit insurance dispute. IAG said in a new update today that its subsidiary Insurance Australia Limited (IAL) had agreed to settle the Credit Suisse proceedings in the Federal Court of Australia. The aggregate face value of the claims was approximately A$2.8bn plus interest, although IAG said the settlement would have no material impact on its financial position or FY27 financial results because of anticipated recoveries under insurance and reinsurance arrangements and other indemnities.

item.title: Pacific Life Re appoints Mei Sum Chan as Head of Medical Analytics
item.description: Global life reinsurer Pacific Life Re has announced the appointment of Mei Sum Chan as Head of Medical Analytics. Pacific Life Re noted that Medical Analytics plays an important role in helping it understand emerging health and mortality trends, supporting assumption development and delivering data-driven insights for its business and clients. Sum Chan succeeds Ian Collins, who retires following more than 15 years at Pacific Life Re.

item.title: People Moves: Garcia Joins InsurBanc as President and CEO
item.description: InsurBanc , headquartered in Farmington, Connecticut, named Lou Garcia as president and CEO. Garcia brings more than 25 years of leadership experience in investment banking, alternative asset management and financial services to his new role at InsurBanc. Garcia has been a vice president at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, which was acquired by Credit Suisse in 2000, and a vice president at JH Whitney & Co., one of the country’s oldest private equity firms.

item.title: Texas Woman Pleads Guilty to Setting House on Fire
item.description: A Wharton County, Texas woman pleaded guilty to setting a house fire in July and was sentenced to 10 years deferred adjudication, the Texas State Fire Marshall Office announced. The Wharton County Sheriff’s Office arrested Rylie Bean in February at the scene of a burglary and house fire. item.title: New York Sues Polymarket, Says It Ran Illegal Gambling Operation
item.description: New York’s attorney general sued Polymarket on Thursday, escalating her battle against prediction markets, an industry that she says violates state laws against illegal gambling. Attorney General Letitia James filed her petition nearly two months after bringing a similar case against Polymarket rival Kalshi. She filed similar petitions i n April against two other prediction market operators, Coinbase Financial Markets and Gemini Titan James’ case against Polymarket is the latest effort by US states to crack down on an industry that has soared in popularity since faring better than pollsters in predicting that Republican Donald Trump would beat Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election.

item.title: EV Sales Are Booming in Europe With Gasoline at $10 a Gallon
item.description: After years of broadly unsuccessful efforts to wean drivers off combustion engines, sales of electric vehicles are surging in Europe thanks to the jump in fuel prices stoked by geopolitical upheaval. The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is disrupting tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the average price of a liter of gasoline in Germany to a record €2.31 a liter (equivalent to $10 per gallon). Germany, the biggest market, led the gains with a three-quarter jump while sales in France more than doubled.

item.title: Online Insurance Marketplace Insurify Blocks Meta’s Personal AI Agent Muse
item.description: 23, the online insurance marketplace said it was cutting off a different personal AI agent. Meta’s Muse has been blocked from accessing Insurify’s comparison platform because the information the AI agent spits out “risks stripping carrier quotes of critical contextual information that consumers need to make informed insurance-buying decisions,” Insurify said. We support AI agents that make insurance shopping better, but they need to preserve the information and consumer control required to make an informed insurance decision.” The spokesperson said Insurify has no exclusive relationship with ChatGPT, and the decision to block Muse was may not be exclusive either.

item.title: Europe Energy Chief Warns of Growing Risk of Attacks on Infrastructure
item.description: Companies must prepare for successful attacks on critical power infrastructure as both physical and cyber threats continue to increase, the CEO of E.ON, Europe’s largest operator of energy grids, said on Thursday. “Attacks on our grids are increasing significantly,” Leonhard Birnbaum told an industry conference, adding that both physical and cyber attacks had increased in recent years. Birnbaum said companies should abandon the idea that they could fully shield themselves from attacks and rather focus on preparation, pointing to the fact that grid assets are high in numbers and geographically spread.

item.title: Cargo Theft a Top Concern for Majority of Retail Loss Control Leaders
item.description: A new survey of 150 U.S.-based loss and organized retail crime prevention leaders finds that 81% report it has become more organized in recent years, while 79% say their organization is more concerned about cargo theft than ever before, according to SmartSense by Digi’s Cargo Theft Report. More than half of respondents (63%) said cargo theft incidents have increased compared with last year and 81% said that organized retail crime is a growing concern for their organization. New forms of instantaneous location tracking and visibility intelligence are needed to understand what normal movement looks like, identify anomalies quickly and act before suspicious activity turns into a multimillion-dollar loss.” When asked about cargo theft tactics, respondents identified fraudulent pickups and carrier impersonation (78%), GPS jamming and spoofing (71%), trailer theft (66%), and double brokering (64%) as their top concerns.

item.title: Affordable and accessible reinsurance remains critical to Florida market’s stability: Morningstar DBRS
item.description: Given Florida’s significant exposure to hurricane risk, a new report from Morningstar DBRS has suggested that continued access to affordable and readily available reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength. “Given Florida’s significant hurricane exposure, continued access to affordable and readily available reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength.” Morningstar DBRS also stressed that the remainder of the 2026 hurricane season will still be an important test of recent market improvements. Over the longer term, the market’s sustainability will depend heavily on the industry’s ability to generate adequate returns while maintaining coverage that remains accessible and reasonably affordable for Florida residents.” In addition, the report also highlights how reinsurance market conditions in Florida have also drastically improved in recent years, following the stressed environment that it experienced during the height of the Florida market disruption.

item.title: ILS should be seen as a source of ‘strategic possibility’ not just capital: Aeolus’ Dutt
item.description: Aditya Dutt, President of Aeolus Capital Management, has indicated that the re/insurance industry is not making full use of the insurance-linked securities (ILS) investor base by treating the market as just a source of capital, where it should also be viewing it as a source of “strategic possibility”. People who issue stock, nothing against it, but you don’t know who they are, and you can’t pick up the phone and call your shareholders and say, ‘Hey, what do you think of doing this transaction together?’ “And I think the most underutilised aspect of the ILS industry is this notion that it’s a source of capital, and not a source of strategic possibility.” Dutt also added that the size of the investor base in ILS means the opportunity goes well beyond simply offering investors new lines of business. But opening the door to strategic possibility really expands the opportunity set of what we can do.” During the webinar, Dutt also called the role of third-party capital “critical,” saying: “It’s growing, and its capabilities are expanding.

item.title: Sedgwick launches Carrier and Captive Solutions offering
item.description: Sedgwick, a global provider of technology-enabled risk, claims and business solutions, has launched its new Carrier and Captive Solutions entity, designed to manage claims complexity, improve performance and support long-term growth. Jason Rogers will lead the offering as Managing Director, Carrier and Captive Solutions. “With the industry’s largest team of dedicated professionals, a claims dataset five times larger than that of the nearest competitor, and trusted strategic partnerships with more than 130 carriers, we can provide a level of depth this market hasn’t had before.” Sedgwick’s Carrier and Captive Solutions combines workers’ compensation expertise across all 50 states and is part of an organisation handling 1.2 million liability claims annually.

item.title: ANV appoints Sarthak Sharma to lead US Transactional Risk business

Sharma joins ANV with almost 10 years of experience in insurance and law, including work across transactional risk, underwriting and mergers and acquisitions.

item.title: Reinsurers eye specialty lines to drive growth as property cat rates soften: Berenberg
item.description: Reinsurers are shifting their growth focus from core catastrophe markets toward high-barrier specialty lines as property catastrophe rates face continued softening, according to Berenberg comments following the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre. Berenberg observed that even though property cat cover is absorbing the market’s steepest rate declines – which in part reflects its profitability since 2023 -, US property cat remains attractive for reinsurers. Outside traditional cat lines, reinsurers’ focus for growth includes speciality lines and, within speciality lines, construction and engineering risks, as well as credit and surety.

item.title: Singapore Court Strips Control of Radiant World From Founder
item.description: A Singapore court appointed KPMG restructuring executives to take charge of Radiant World on Thursday, granting an application by creditor Mizuho Bank Ltd., which has accused the trader of alleged fraud linked to iron ore receivables. The decision removes Radiant World founder Pinkesh Nahar’s control over the group’s key operating entity, opening a new chapter in a saga that has gripped the global commodities industry since Bloomberg first reported in July on concerns that it had been using falsified documents to raise money from banks. KPMG executives Toh Ai Ling, Adrian Chan and Tan Yen Chiaw will be interim judicial managers of Radiant World Corporation Pte., the trader’s key operating entity in Singapore, according to people familiar with the court’s decision, which was communicated on Thursday.
